source: MIL-STD-882E categories; cell assignments are this repository's own, stricter than the standard in places by design. This file is the single source of truth for the 4x5 impact matrix: the table in REVIEW_LAWS.md equals it (a test checks), and repo-side copies of REVIEW_LAWS.md copy that table.

action_meaning.H: hold the pull request for the captain

owner_hold.meaning: Which holds need the owner's own clear. Only a change to credentials, identity or who may do what holds for the owner; every other floor path or rating asks for a second independent review and the usual checks decide the merge. The code reads this block and has no path or class list of its own.

narrow_by_diff.meaning: Paths whose hold depends on their CONTENT: an agent definition holds for the owner only when its permission block changes between the base and the head of the pull request (the top level front matter keys named here); an added, removed or unreadable definition holds, and so does a pull request that changes more than max_files of them. The code has no path or key of its own.

authority_modules.meaning: Every module in bin/ that defines a function whose name has a word of `vocabulary` (names split at underscores) decides who may clear, hold, release, carry, consent to, record a verdict for or merge something, so it must be a top tier path above or be named in `exempt` with the reason it is not. A test reads this block and fails, naming the module, when a module is neither. The vocabulary is data: adding a word here widens the guard with no code change. A SECOND rule does not look at names: a module with a comparison (==, !=, in, not in) against one of the `role_literals` (the role names the fleet checks a caller by) decides who may act, so it must be listed or exempted too; a renamed function cannot hide it. When in doubt, LIST: an exemption needs a reason a reviewer can verify. `limits` says what the guard cannot see.

exempt.bin/path_suites.py: gate_finding words an INFORMATION line (a pull request changes a path and names none of the suites that exercise it). Trace: its only caller is the gates finding in bin/fleet-switchboard, which prints the line for people to read and never changes a gate verdict; no role, tier, identity, verdict, clear or merge is produced or read (ask #1045).
exempt.bin/agent_calls.py: release_notice gives back a once-an-hour message claim for an account's budget notice. Trace: its only caller is the budget notice command in bin/fleet-switchboard, which calls it after claim_notice when the reminder could not be added; it truncates a rate-limit file in the state directory and returns nothing, so no role, tier, identity, verdict or clear is produced or read.
exempt.bin/plan_approval.py: `evaluate` returns the verdict and the one stderr line of a refused approval. Trace: its only caller is `check_approval` in bin/fleet-switchboard (the send command), which prints the line and records an approval only after a GET-only read of the plan comment; the module is pure, reads and writes nothing, and returns no role, tier, identity or clear, and nothing in bin/ reads its result as one. Exemption reason: refusal-only; no clear or hold depends on plan.approved; list it as an authority module if a clear ever depends on plan.approved.
exempt.bin/spotlight_guard.py: holds_files tells whether a folder holds an entry. Trace: used only inside bin/spotlight_guard.py (the Spotlight index check of ask #438); the module returns no role, tier, identity, verdict or clear, and nothing in bin/ reads its result as one.
exempt.bin/triage_digest.py: gate is a rate limit on the stale digest (warm-up and interval). Trace: its only caller is the triage digest in bin/fleet-switchboard, where `allowed` decides whether a digest message is SENT now; no role, tier, verdict or clear is produced or read.
exempt.bin/triage_plan_open.py: merged_links reads which links a merged unit names. Trace: its callers are the triage's plan-open check in bin/fleet-switchboard, which only lists findings for people to read; nothing it returns reaches answer_authority, a caller check, a verdict or a clear.

limits: The guard reads function NAMES (underscore-separated words) and COMPARISONS (==, !=, in, not in) against the role literals, in the .py files of bin/ only.

It cannot see: a role held in a constant or variable and compared by that name; a check written with startswith, endswith, a regular expression, match/case or a dictionary lookup; a literal built at run time; code that is not a .py file in bin/ (bin/fleet-switchboard, scripts, shims, plugins, agents); a value that is PRODUCED by an unlisted module and later read by an authority function (a producer trace is the reviewer's).

The fallback: the strict review (the independent reviewer) looks for exactly these, as R-LAW-12 and the owner-hold rule say, and an exemption must carry a trace of where its values go. When in doubt, LIST.

owner_hold.note: top_tier_outside_floor lists the top tier paths that are deliberately not in the floor globs (the floor excludes agent definitions, which are captain pull requests); a test checks that every other top tier path is inside the floor. bin/fleet-switchboard selects accounts and mints tokens but is not a top tier path (it would hold nearly every change): a change there to credentials or identity must be rated with that class by the independent review.
owner_hold.never_carried_meaning: The owner's clear is NEVER carried over a merge of main that resolved a conflict by hand (bin/clear_carry.py, bin/impact_hold.py: the carry reads this list through impact_floor.carry_never_paths and holds no path of its own) when that merge touches one of these paths or the pull request's own change does: the clear's own code and this matrix. Credential and identity paths are not here: they are carried like any other path (the owner's answer, ask #815). Every exact path of `delegated_clear.clear_code_paths` is here, because the ledger and the plan check decide who may confirm a carry; its directory globs (the plugin, the shims, the templates, the proof tools, the workflows) are not, and the shims are identity paths the owner chose to carry. A test checks both lists against each other and that every bin module named for the clear, the hold or the floor is here. The guard for what is not listed (the daemon file, the globs) is the independent reviewer's confirmation and the continuous tests, not a proof.

delegated_clear.meaning: What the Chief of Staff's clear under the owner's standing order may NEVER lift (bin/delegated_clear.py reads this block and holds no path, class or function name of its own). For an order WITHOUT a `max_level`, two refusals apply. The first refuses a pull request whose top tier path hits include a class of `never_path_classes`. The second refuses a pull request whose independent review's class is one of `top_tier_review_classes` (or none is recorded). For an order WITH a `max_level`, the score rule in `score` replaces those two refusals. The refusals below apply either way, with or without a `max_level`. A pull request that changes ANY file matching `clear_code_paths` (the clear and hold machinery by name, and the directories the daemon and the CLI load at start) is refused: never delegated also means ALWAYS HELD for the owner, because the floor holds a pull request that changes one of them (the code the clear merely loads, `closure_files`, is outside that hold until the closure ask #940 lands). A pull request that ADDS, DELETES or RENAMES a file matching `new_file_globs` (a new file under bin/ is loaded at config load) is refused. A pull request that changes a file of `closure_files` (the daemon file and the bin modules the clear loads or runs (the daemon's imports at load, the config readers every module declares, and a recorded run of the clear: a test derives the list); for a module other than the daemon file ANY import-time statement, and the functions of `module_roots`) on a line that belongs to the CLEAR CLOSURE is refused: the definitions reachable by name from `closure_roots`, the module-level bindings they read, any other top-level statement, or a definition that refers to a `clear_entry_points` name. Other changes under bin/ (an authority module edit that does not change who may do what) are allowed.

score.meaning: The score rule (#835), used for an order that sets max_level: the score is the highest LEVEL of the matrix's cells for the independent impact reviewer's records at the pull request's exact head, on the ladder below. A changed path of a top tier class (the rule ids below name the classes) makes `floor.lowest_level` the lowest score allowed: a rating below it on such a path is refused, and the rating's reason must name the rule id. Only a level of `delegable_levels` may be cleared: High is always the owner's. Only a record whose recorded role is in `rating_roles` counts. The clear code holds no level, rule id or role of its own.
